anger angels (ETERNAL LETDOWN) is the first collaboration between choreographers and artists Teresa Vittucci and Sophia Rodriguez. In this hypnotic, humorous and visceral performance they explore anger as a transformative, even celestial energy.

Set within a surreal, corporate-inspired landscape, the two become angelic messengers that navigate and process human rage. These angels are not serene beings, but active catalysts like listeners, warriors and translators between worlds. Through movement, voice and sincere irony, they transform anger into something luminous and liberating. Experiencing anger angels (ETERNAL LETDOWN) feels like receiving a deep tissue massage you did not know you needed: both unsettling and strangely soothing.

• Sophía Rodríguez (1984, VE/BE, she/her) is an actress, dancer, choreographer, and circus artist. She has studied circus, dance, and physical theatre in Venezuela (Universidad Experimental de las Artes), Cuba (Cuban National Circus School), and Switzerland (Accademia Dimitri). Her long-term exchange and training with David Zambrano has had a strong influence on her artistic practice. As a creator, she uses physical performance, embodied knowledge, voice, and improvisation as building blocks for energetic, feminist, and critical performances that always balance between disciplines. Kaaitheater previously presented her FRICTION (2023), in collaboration with Charleroi Danse.

Tiago Rodrigues draws inspiration from a true story about his father. Rogério Rodrigues, a respected Portuguese journalist, began writing a newspaper article during his final days in the hospital. Every day, his father worked in his notebook on a story about his experiences as a terminal patient. Both Tiago and his father knew this would be his last article.

After his father's death, Tiago opened the notebook. It contained only a few lines and dots, a few scribbles, like the abstract drawings of a toddler. Now, Tiago wants to depict those unwritten pages of his father's final work. By combining memories, songs, and fragments of his father's writings, he builds a performance that aims to be a small victory over death.

Each scene is a playful variation on the theme of parting. The stage forms a surreal landscape in which hospital beds glide across an icy sea, as a metaphor for the tumult of life. With music and poetry as the grammar of a theatre that can find joy in even the saddest stories.

• The first ambition of Portuguese actor and director Tiago Rodrigues was to perform with people who wanted to create shows together. His encounter with the Belgian theatre company tg Stan in 1997, at the age of 20, definitively confirmed his attachment to the absence of hierarchy in a creative group. There he developed his acting, dramatic writing and love for the collective.
